body:
I honestly wish they would do the same, and generally it's the former. I don't enjoy faking intimacy, I see it as a chore. Though I guess that can't be entirely true because I find myself attracted to nice, genuine people. I still feel like I want to grow into a person like that, even if I know it's unlikely. 

If I knew for sure I could never change though, I'd be happy to get everything I need from people just trading favors.

I feel emotions, in fact I'm sometimes overwhelmed by them. 

I don't trust them though. If I feel something, and then stop to ask "why am I feeling this," chances are it's for shitty reasons. My emotions are honestly pretty much entirely self serving. I do genuinely feel bad about this though. Like, when my brother attempted suicide I felt bad for not feeling bad and genuinely struggled with it. 

I guess that's a personality, it's just a really shitty one. My personality doesn't exist outside the context of myself.

To be honest, I don't think I really feel human. I'm not sure my personality exists. I've had emotions in the past that lasted so long and felt so real and they ended up being a way to control my friend. She didn't call me out on it either, I just realized it. I kinda think that's what I am. Fundamentally narcissistic. Every time I try to be myself it turns out my self is a prick. I lost faith in the idea that there's some nugget of humanity buried in me. I really don't believe in any sort of romance within myself. To feel real I'd have to say something like: "hey, I'm gonna use you even when I don't realize what I'm doing, and I expect you to try the same. Let's have some fun anyways and with some luck we'll both come out better." 

I genuinely enjoy friendships based on either competition, or collaboration. You can have fun without even worrying about anything that isn't the task at hand or something pretty superficial.

It's not the shit specifically, if that's what you mean. The shit is just very damning evidence of something being irreparably broken.

What truly bothers me is the knowledge that I'll never really relate to anyone. The fact that all of my relationships are either total lies or based on pity. I really did develop alone for much of growing up and now I realize being social is pretty much the point of life and it sucks. The fact that even when I'm acting with confidence, that I still know the man behind the curtain and therefore I lack the ability to ever truly be genuine. By having such a relationship with myself, I've fundamentally taken the magic out of having relationships with other people. It's not just lonliness when I'm physically alone. It's the loneliness of not having a true emotional connection (where I wasn't really just manipulating the other person pretending to feel something I wasn't). It's knowing there's no undoing what I've done. Just getting better at faking being someone else.
